exposure: type of anesthesia (spinal anesthesia with morphine vs. other methods)
outcome: opioid analgesic utilization (morphine milligram equivalents - MME)
cohort: The study included 46 pregnant women prescribed buprenorphine who delivered by cesarean section, compared to matched controls not on medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD).
finding: Women on buprenorphine undergoing cesarean section utilized more opioid analgesics (MME) but had similar pain scores compared to matched controls not on MOUD.
mod_finding: Among women on buprenorphine, those who received spinal anesthesia with morphine had lower pain scores during the first 48 hours postpartum compared to those receiving other methods of anesthesia during cesarean section.
